posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
I think Story War is a great game. If you enjoy spinning tales and beating others, you might love it. It's a very creative game and has great artwork and quality cards. The rules are easy to learn. You can jump right into the game.

I found the game more frustrating than fun the one time I played. I like making stuff up, but not having other people tell me why my ideas are wrong. I like winning, but not telling other people that their ideas are wrong. When I'm making stuff up, I enjoy being whimsical and free to explore my creativity. Having to come up with a better story than others put me into analysis mode instead, which might be ok, but it was in a situation where the way to win was only partly about logic, while also being significantly about persuasion.

posts.name: Bas
posts.cooked:
Amnachaidh:

We own and enjoy "Once Upon a Time", which is a vaugely similar game

To spice up the player interaction within "Once upon a Time", I added 10 custom cards; 5x "Erase", which could nullify/erase the card an opponent played, thus leaving a hole in the story that needed to be filled up by the player (throwing them off guard), and 5x "Replace", which allowed a player to replace a card played by an opponent by one of a similar type from their hand. Worked quite nicely to keep the more shy people involved in the game-aspect, without having to take over the storyline.

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
10 pts to Pydro.

I find Dixit and Apples to Apples to be poles apart; the latter is a great laugh with a non-gaming crowd and has been a dinner party staple of ours for a long time, but I don't think I'll ever play it again with a full on gaming group. I guess it depends on if you try to play it like an actual game, or just shoot for rewarding the funniest suggestions, as it ends up being a very different experience. I like Dixit but personally don't enjoy it when it devolves into single word 'clues' or obscure references designed for only one other person to be able to get, I prefer telling an actual one or two sentence short story as it opens up the possible interpretations of the cards so much more.

In other news, I tried Mysterium recently and I have to say that I much prefer it to Dixit, there seems to be more of a game going on. Definitely worth a look in if you like Dixit.
